sample_10.text: Good morning. I am Dr. Norgard.
We have not met before. Could I have your name, please?
Good morning. Be it a Reese.
Welcome, Beirta. Please have a seat. What can I help you with today?
I need my prescriptions renewed. The asthma medicine and the one for stomach acid.
Of course. Before we do that, has anything new turned up? Any new symptoms?
No, nothing new. Should there be? I do worry about the asthma sometimes.
That is a fair thing to wonder about. Nothing you have described today points to something new.
It is the allergic kind of asthma I have. Is that right?
Yes, allergic asthma. That is the condition we are treating.
I just want to be sure it is not quietly getting worse.
Then let us listen to your chest and your heart, and we will know more about today.
Yes, please do.
Breathe normally for me. And once more?
Is everything all right?
Your lungs and your heart both sound normal.
Nothing abnormal on listening.
That is a relief to hear.
I would describe this as a stable situation.
You do need to continue the treatment you are on.
So I carry on with everything exactly as before?
Exactly as before. And I will renew both prescriptions today.
Which ones will that be?
Dimista and Esomeprizol for the stomach acid. Both renewed.
Thank you. That is what I was hoping for.
Did you notice the first frost this morning?
I did. The car windows were completely white.
Autumn has made its point rather firmly.
It has. Right, so I only need to collect the medicine.
That is all. Anything else before you go?
No, I think that is everything. Thank you, doctor.
Take care, Beirutah. Goodbye.

sample_17.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Skov. We have not met before. You are Suzan Hiyot.
Yes, good morning.
Welcome. Please sit down. Did you get here all right?
The bus was delayed, but I still made it in time.
Then the day is off to a decent start.
You are here for the answer on the swap from your mouth.
Yes, that is why I came.
I have it in front of me.
The swap shows yeast fungi.
So it is a fungal infection.
It is. A fungal infection in the mouth,
and it is one that needs treating.
What does the treatment involve?
Sporanox, 100 milligrams daily for two weeks.
You take it after a meal.
After a meal every day for two weeks.
Exactly right. Always after food.
All right, that is clear.
Any questions about it?
No, I do not think so.
Good. Have you been baking anything new lately?
I try to rye loaf at the weekend.
It turned out better than I expected.
That is a fine result. Take care, Suzan.
Thank you. Goodbye.

sample_18.text: Morning, Dr. Scove. Thanks for fitting me in.
Morning, Yens. Always good to see you.
Busy out there with the school holidays.
Very. The whole town seems to be on the move.
It is like that every summer.
So, what can I do for you?
I need my ibumet and renewed.
All right.
And you are still taking pantop result alongside it?
Yes, every day with it.
Good.
Now, one thing I want to be open with you about.
You have used anti-inflammatory painkillers heavily and for a long time.
Is that harming me?
It means we should monitor your blood pressure and your kidney function.
That is the sensible step.
How do we go about that?
I would like you to measure your blood pressure at home over three days.
I can do that. And the kidneys?
Blood tests. Please book a time for those.
We check kidneys, cholesterol and blood sugar.
And you will still renew the ibumet in today?
Yes, the prescription is created.
Does that plan sound workable to you?
It does. Home readings for three days, then the blood tests.
That is it.
Have you read anything good lately?
I finished a crime novel last night.
It kept me up far too late.
The good ones tend to.
Take care, Yens.
Thanks. See you.

sample_19.text: Good afternoon. My name is Signe Everson. I have not been here before.
Welcome. I'm Dr. Fabriceus. Please sit down. Did you get away from work easily?
Yes, thank you. It has been a busy day, but I managed.
Good. What do you need today?
Two prescriptions renewed. Active L and Aromere. If that is alright.
That is fine. Anything else?
I am still being treated for asthma and for reflux.
Noted. Both are ongoing.
Is it a problem that I have been on them for so long?
No. Your medication is stable.
Stable meaning it is doing what it should.
Yes. Nothing suggests a change is needed.
Alright. I do worry about the asthma sometimes.
Understandable. Today we continue your treatment.
So you are not concerned about anything?
Not from what you have told me. Your medication is stable.
Right. Sorry for asking twice.
It is no trouble at all.
Which prescriptions will I get?
Active L, Aromere, and Isomeprizol. All three renewed.
The Isomeprizol is the one for the reflux.
Yes, that is right.
Good. That is what I take.
Anything else before you go?
No, that is everything.
The supermarket was packed this morning so I am glad to sit down.
Everyone seems to shop at the same hour.
Take care, Signe.
Thank you, doctor. Goodbye.

sample_20.text: Good morning. My name is Niels Everson.
I hope this is the right room. The corridor out there is a bit of a maze.
You found it. I am Dr. Poulson. Good to meet you.
Please take a seat, and we will go through things in order.
Thank you. Since we have not met before, I will start from the beginning if that suits you.
Please do. Tell me what brings you here today, and afterwards I will explain my assessment and the plan.
Well, it is quite simple, really. I have almost run out of my painkillers, and I was hoping to have the prescriptions renewed.
Which painkillers are we talking about? I would like to hear you name them yourself.
Pamol and ibumetin. Those of the two I use, and I have been taking them for a good while now.
Thank you. Pamol is paracetamol, and ibumetin belongs to the anti-inflammatory painkillers.
Does that match how you think of them?
It does, more or less. In my head, one of them is the mild everyday one, and the other is the stronger one for inflammation.
That is a fair way to put it. And the pain itself, where would you say it sits?
That is the awkward part. It is not one spot at all. It is a general wide spread sort of pain, spread around the body rather than in one place.
General or wide spread pain is exactly the heading I would use for it. Has anything about it changed recently?
No, not really. It is much the same as it has been. Steady, I suppose, is the word. Nothing new has turned up to alarm me.
Good. Then we are looking at a stable pain problem, with a continued need for pain relief.
That is a relief to hear. Oh, before I forget, have you seen anything worth watching lately?
I finally finished a series my neighbor kept pushing on me.
I have little time for television, but I watched a film last weekend that was worth the evening. How was your series?
Slow to begin with, honestly. But it grew on me, and by the end I was recommending it to everyone.
Patience pays off, apparently. Patience is a rare commodity. Let us come back to the medication side of things.
Yes, of course. Do you want to examine me first? I have expected that.
Not today. Today is about the medication, so there is no examination to record from this visit.
All right, I will admit I am not sorry about that. So what is your conclusion then?
That your pain problem is stable and that you still need pain relieving medication. Nothing about the treatment needs changing.
So I simply carry on exactly as I have been doing?
Yes, I am creating prescriptions for both Pamol and Ibu Metin now, and they will be waiting for you at the pharmacy.
That is a weight off my mind. I was down to the last few tablets in the box, and I did not fancy running out over a weekend.
Then the timing is good. Is there any part of the plan you would like me to go over again?
No, I think it is clear. Renewed prescriptions for both and nothing else changes.
One practical thing though, I came by bicycle and left it against the railing at the front.
There is a proper rack around the side of the building, a little more sheltered. Most people leave theirs there.
I will move it on my way out then. Thank you very much for your time.
You are welcome, Niels. Take care.

sample_23.text: Morning Yens, you came through that downpour I see.
I did. It went sideways the last hundred meters. I nearly turned back.
Glad you did not. What brings you in?
Some skin changes that keep bothering me.
One under my right breast, a couple on my stomach,
and one on my left lower leg. I want them gone.
Let me look at them.
The one under your right breast is a skin wart about one centimeter.
And you can tell that just by looking at it?
Yes, it has the appearance of one.
The others on your abdomen and lower leg are 0.6 centimeters,
scaly, and brownish.
Scaly and brownish covers a lot of ground. What do you think they are?
They look like seboria caratosis. That is a common harmless growth.
Look like, so you are not certain.
I am describing what I see. My assessment is that these are benign skin changes.
benign all of them, including the one under the breast.
Yes, that is my assessment of all of them.
Fair enough, then can we get on with removing them?
We can. I will arrange an appointment for the removal.
And what am I signing up for? I would rather hear the downside now.
There will be a scar where each one is removed, and there is a risk of infection afterwards.
You should know both before we book it.
Right, a scar and an infection risk.
I would still rather have them off than keep catching them.
Understood. Then the appointment for removal is the plan.
Good. Any idea whether this weather holds through the weekend?
The forecast says it clears by Saturday. Take care, Yens.

sample_33.text: Good morning. My name is Morton Reese. I have an appointment.
Good morning Morton. I'm Dr. Bang. Please have a seat.
Thank you. I was not sure I had found the right room.
You have. This is your follow-up for allergic rhinitis.
Yes. I have been worrying about whether it is really under control.
Let us go through it together. How has the medication been?
It has helped. I do not have any symptoms right now.
No symptoms at all at the moment.
None. And that is partly what makes me uneasy.
Say a little more about that if you can.
It feels too easy. I keep thinking something is being missed.
I understand. The examination I have done is normal.
Normal in all of it?
Yes. Nothing abnormal was found on examination.
All right. So the medicine is genuinely working?
Yes. The antihistamine is having a good effect.
So I feel well because of the antihistamine.
That is my assessment.
Do I stop taking it now?
The plan is to continue it as needed.
As needed. So only when the symptoms come back?
Yes. You take it when you need it.
Right. That is clearer now.
Good. I noticed you looking at the plants when you came in.
I was. They look a great deal healthier than mine at home.
The room was rearranged recently too, in case it looked unfamiliar.
It did, a little.
Thank you for explaining everything so patiently.
You are welcome, Morton. Take care.

sample_37.text: Morning, Dr. Norgard. Good to see you again.
Morning, Rasmus. Come in. What brings you today?
I found a tick attached to my leg. I removed it and I wanted the bite looked at.
Right. A tick bite. Any redness around the sight?
No redness at all.
Any swelling?
No swelling, either. The area looks unchanged to me.
Let me have a look at it.
Of course.
The skin is intact. There is no erythema migrants.
So no expanding ring-shaped rash around the bite?
Correct. No erythema migrants.
And how do you rate the risk of berelia?
Low. The risk of berelia here is low.
What are you basing that on?
Intact skin, no redness, no swelling, and no rash at the sight.
Then what is the plan?
Observation. No treatment is needed.
So no antibiotics today?
No. This is an insect bite without complication.
Understood. The mornings have turned properly autumnal, haven't they?
They have. The light goes quickly at this time of year.
I have already dug out the winter jacket.
Sensable. Anything else on your mind today?
No, that was the only thing.
Good. Big plans for the rest of the day?
Just a couple of errands, then some reading at home.
Sounds calm. Take care, Rasmus.
Thanks, Dr. Norgard. Goodbye.

sample_39.text: Good morning, I am Dr. Anderson.
I do not think we have met before.
Did you notice the waiting area?
It was repainted a few weeks ago.
I did, it looks a lot brighter than I expected.
Right, tell me what brings you in today.
Pain in my lower back, it feels muscular.
Does the pain travel anywhere, down into a leg, for example?
No, it stays in the lower back.
I would like to examine your back and see how it moves.
I can feel tight, tender bands in the muscles.
Your movement is also reduced when you bend and turn.
Putting it together, this is non-specific muscle and joint pain in the back without radiation.
For treatment, I recommend pain relief and an exercise program.
The exercises are the part that keeps the back moving.

sample_4.text: Morning, Doctor Fabricius.
Christian, come in. Good to see you.
You too. I see the magazines in the waiting room have finally been refreshed.
They had been there so long I was starting to recognize the covers.
I read one all the way through, which tells you something.
It tells me we are running on time for once.
So this is your annual follow-up.
It is, for the asthma.
Exactly that.
Let me listen to your chest and your heart and then we will talk.
Go ahead.
Breathe normally for me and again.
Is it all right?
Your chest and heart both sound normal.
Nothing abnormal to report.
Good. I had half convinced myself something would turn up this year.
Nothing has. This is what a stable annual check looks like.
So what happens with my treatment?
No changes. You carry on exactly as you are.
Nothing at all. I suppose I expected some adjustment.
There is nothing to adjust.
When the follow-up is clear, leaving things alone is the right call.
That is reassuring to hear said plainly.
Then that is the whole of it.
Asthma follow-up done. No changes.
Shorter than I had booked out for.
The good ones usually are.
Everything busier at your end with the school holidays.
Considerably, the roads at 8 in the morning are a different world.
It is the same here.
The mornings fill up the moment term ends.
Then I will let you get on. Thank you.
Take care Christian. Same time next year.

sample_42.text: Good morning, Camilla. Come in and sit down.
Thank you. It is nice to be back.
I always forget how calm it is in here compared with everything going on outside.
It has its moments. This is your preventive health check today.
Yes, that is right. And I have to say, I feel perfectly well.
No complaints at all, which almost feels like cheating.
That is worth noting. Feeling well is part of the picture.
Good. I did wonder whether coming in when nothing is actually wrong was a waste of your time.
Not at all. That is exactly what these checks are for.
Fair enough. So what did you find?
Your blood pressure is 135 over 88.
135 over 88. I will be honest, those figures mean very little to me on their own.
That is the reading I measured today.
Right. And was there anything else you measured?
Your body mass index is 28.
28. And what does that tell you?
It puts you in the mildly overweight range.
Mildly overweight. I suspected as much, honestly. Clothes tell you before the scales do.
That is my assessment. And I would not put it more strongly than that.
I appreciate that. I have had people be far more dramatic about far less.
There is no need for drama here.
So what happens next? Is there something I should be doing?
The plan is advice on diet and on exercise.
Diet and exercise. The two words everybody expects to hear and yet here we are.
They are the plan for today. That is fine by me.
I would far rather have advice than a prescription.
Understood. The seasons are turning already. I notice the light is different in the mornings now.
And everything smells like the end of summer.
It does come round quickly. It does. I always mean to make more of the summer.
And then, quite suddenly, it is gone.
Most of us do exactly the same. That is comforting.
Now, back to my results for a moment. Of course.
The mildly overweight assessment. That was based on the body mass index.
Yes, on the body mass index of 28.
Understood. And that is everything for today.
What I have for you today is the blood pressure, the body mass index and the advice.
Right. Well, that is manageable enough.
What are your plans for the rest of the day?
Nothing dramatic. I might walk home the long way,
seeing as we have been talking about exercise.
That sounds like a good start. Take care, Camilla.
Thank you. See you next time.

sample_43.text: Hello, Trini. Good to see you. Have a seat.
Thanks. My throat has been really sore.
A sore throat. Let us take it in order. First, I did a test on your throat.
A test. What sort of test is that?
A strap test. It looks for one particular bacterium that can cause a sore throat.
And what did it say?
It was negative. That means that bacterium was not found.
So negative is the good one here?
In this case, yes. I also looked at your throat and there was no pus.
No pus. That is the yellow stuff you sometimes get?
That is right. There was none of it.
So what is making it hurt then?
My assessment is that this is a viral infection.
A virus. Not bacteria then.
Exactly. Does that difference make sense to you?
I think so. So do I need antibiotics for it?
No. The plan is no antibiotics because they do not work against a virus.
All right. So what do I do instead?
We treat the symptoms, so we ease the discomfort while it passes.
Just making it feel better, basically.
Yes. That is a good way to put it.
The road works nearly made me late getting here by the way.
They have caught a lot of people out this week.
They have. Is the weekend meant to be any good?
The forecast looks decent from what I have seen.
That is something. Thanks for explaining it all so clearly.
You are welcome, Trini. Take care of that throat.

sample_47.text: Thank you for squeezing me in today.
It is really sore and it hurts when I swallow.
A sore throat and pain on swallowing.
It has been worrying me a bit if I am honest.
Let us have a proper look and we can go from there.
Your tonsils are red and there is coating on them.
It is a whitish layer sitting on the surface of the tonsils.
And the redness is that part of the same thing?
Yes, the redness and the coating on the tonsils go together here.
So what do you think it is?
So an infection of the tonsils.
That is exactly what it means.
I had convinced myself it was something worse.
And what happens about treating it?
I am starting you on penicillin treatment.
I like knowing that something is being done.
Did you have to wait long out there?
Although I did get through most of a magazine in the waiting room.
They are older than any of us would like to admit.
I did notice the dates on them.
Is there anything else about your throat?
The coating you saw is that what the treatment is for?
The treatment is directed at the tonsilitis.
That is what we are addressing today.
I did not want to promise.
The queue at the pharmacy next door looked enormous
It builds up around this hour.
It usually thins out later on.
Then I will take my time walking over.

sample_48.text: Hello, Kirsten. Come in and sit down. Thank you.
I have been a little nervous about today. I will admit.
Let us take it in order and it will make more sense.
You came about tiredness. Yes, it has been going on and on.
It simply does not lift. Persistent fatigue.
That is what we were investigating. That is it exactly.
And I keep thinking there must be a reason for it.
We tested two things. The first was your thyroid stimulating hormone, the thyroid.
I had wondered about that one. It came back normal, normal.
And the other one? Your glucose, which is your blood sugar.
That was normal as well. Both normal.
So nothing was found at all. Correct.
My assessment is that there is no hormonal cause for the tiredness, no hormonal cause.
Does that mean nothing serious is going on?
It tells us the thyroid and the glucose results are normal.
That is what these tests can say. I see, but I am still tired, so something must be causing it.
I understand that is frustrating. What the tests show is that these results are normal.
Right. So what is the plan then?
No specific treatment is needed on the basis of these results.
Nothing at all. That feels strange when I still feel like this.
I know. That is the plan today based on what we have found.
Does that make sense? I think so. It is just not what I had expected to hear.
That is completely understandable. Sorry.
I have been dwelling on it rather a lot since the tests.
Not at all. The seasons are turning now, which everybody seems to be noticing.
They are. It is getting dark so much earlier already.
And the school holidays have made everything busier as well.
They have. The whole town seems full at the moment.
Take care, Kirsten. Thank you, Dr. Brun.

sample_5.text: Come in, I am Dr. Villidson. We have not met before, I think.
No, we have not. Louise Dahl, lovely to meet you.
I was just saying to the lady outside that the waiting room went far quicker than I expected.
That is good to hear. Take a seat. There is a lot on your list today, so I would like to go through it with you rather than at you.
I appreciate that. Where would you like to start? Probably the back since that is the oldest of it.
The back, yes. This is the chronic pain since your neck operation.
That is right, the cervical disc prolapse operated in 2017.
And honestly, the pain has just carried on regardless.
Despite taking the ibumetin and the panadill regularly,
despite both, and I do take them properly, that is the frustrating part.
And then the anti-inflammatory gave me reflux on top, which is why you are on pan top resolve for that.
Exactly, yes. So one thing patching up the other if you see what I mean.
I do. And your asthma is being followed at the pulmonary outpatient clinic.
It is. And that side of things is genuinely fine.
They keep an eye on it and I have no complaints there.
Good. Then the menopausal symptoms, which you are taking active L4.
Yes. And my hands have started aching as well, which is newer.
I did wonder about arthritis.
Osteoarthritis is what is suspected there. Yes.
Anything else troubling you? Constipation I am afraid.
And I should be honest and say I still smoke. Thank you for saying so.
Let me examine you and then I will tell you what I find.
Please do.
You seem generally unaffected.
Your gait and standing are normal.
I can feel muscle tension in your neck and shoulders.
That tension is exactly where it always sits, right across there.
So to summarize, chronic pain, stable asthma, chronic reflux,
and you are perimenopausal with a need for treatment.
And the hands and the constipation and the smoking.
Osteoarthritis, constipation and nicotine. Yes. All noted.
Now, what would you like to do about the neck and shoulder tension?
If you are about to say physiotherapy, I would rather not.
I have thought about it and it is not for me.
Then we will not refer you.
For the pain, you continue the anti-inflammatory
with the stomach protection alongside it.
And is there anything I need to come back for?
An annual check of your blood pressure.
Does that plan sit right with you?
It does.
And I will say that check-in screen at reception nearly defeated me on the way in.
You are not the first to tell me that today.
Well, I got there in the end.
Thank you, Dr. Villazin.

sample_50.text: Good morning. I am Dr. Anderson. Could you tell me your name, please?
Hana Reese. Nice to meet you.
Likewise. Did you have to wait long at the desk?
A little. The queue was quite long this morning.
It often is at this hour. Let us get started. Have you noticed anything wrong lately?
No. Nothing at all. I feel completely normal.
No symptoms then. Your body mass index is 29.
What does that number mean?
It compares your weight with your height. 29 is above the healthy range.
All right.
Your fasting blood sugar was 7.0 millimoles per liter.
Your long-term sugar value was 47 millimoles per mole.
Is that high? I do not know much about these things.
Both are above normal. Together they raise a suspicion of type 2 diabetes.
Diabetes. So I have it?
It is not confirmed. It is a suspicion.
Further tests have been arranged to settle it.
And those will tell us for certain?
That is why they are being done. Nothing changes for you until we have them.
Okay. I understand.
Good. You had the holiday off I take it. It is only just finished.
Yes. It was quiet and nice, but it went by fast.
They always do. Anything else you want to ask?
No. Thank you doctor. Goodbye.

sample_52.text: Good morning. I am Dr. Winther. And you are?
Gita Nuggle. Good morning.
Welcome. Let us start with what has happened since your last appointment.
I attended the diabetes education course.
Good. Tell me how you found it.
thorough. A lot of it I had already read, but hearing it explained properly helped.
That is often how it works. May I ask what you took away from it?
Mainly a clearer picture of the condition and why the treatment is what it is.
That is exactly the aim of the course.
So what are you assessing today? This feels more like a conversation than a check.
A fair question. With type 2 diabetes, your own understanding of it is part of the treatment.
And you can judge that just from talking to me?
To a degree, yes. From what you describe, you seem engaged and motivated.
That is an impression though, not a measurement.
It is an impression, yes. My assessment is that you have a good understanding of your illness
and your treatment. All right, I can accept that.
Good. Then let me explain what happens next. The plan is continued support and follow-up.
Why continued support if my understanding is already good?
Because this is a long-term condition.
Support keeps that understanding useful over time. And follow-up lets us see how you are doing.
That makes sense.
Is anything about that plan unclear to you?
No, that part is clear.
Good. Are you managing to fit these appointments around work?
Mostly. I take the early slot and go in afterwards.
That works well. Do you drive in?
I cycle usually, though the bike is in for a service this week.
Then walking it is. That is everything for today, Gitta. Take care.
Thank you, doctor. Goodbye.

sample_54.text: Good morning. I am Nana Skol.
Good morning, Nana. I am Dr. Bang. Please take a seat.
Thank you.
I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time.
Not at all. This is your appointment.
What would you like to start with?
Well, I have had my flu vaccination.
Good. Thank you for telling me. That is worth knowing.
I did wonder whether it mattered for the diabetes.
It is part of the routine care, yes.
Now, there are a couple of things I would like to check today.
Of course. It's something wrong.
Nothing that I know of. These are the usual checks.
Let us start with your blood pressure.
All right. Thank you. Your blood pressure is normal.
Oh good. That is a relief.
Now, may I take a look at your feet?
Yes. Should I take off my socks?
Please do. It only takes a moment.
There you are.
Thank you. Your feet are normal.
The examination is fine.
Nothing wrong there, either?
Nothing. Both checks are normal.
That is good to hear.
I do worry about my feet.
That is understandable.
And it is exactly why we look at them.
Today they are fine.
Thank you.
Overall, your diabetes looks stable.
There is nothing here that needs changing.
Stable. So I'm doing all right.
You are. That is my assessment today.
Good.
The plan is continued monitoring,
with your annual check as usual.
Does that sound all right to you?
Yes. I like knowing when things get looked at.
Then that is what we will do.
Any questions about the plan?
No. I think I understand it.
Good.
It is a bright morning out there.
The birds were all over the car park when I arrived.
I noticed them too.
We get a lot of them in the garden at this time of year.
It is a nice thing to look at.
It is.
Then we are finished for today, Nana.
Take care.
Thank you doctor.
Goodbye.

sample_55.text: Morning, Signe. Come in.
Good morning, Dr. Brune.
Sorry, I am a little on edge today.
That is all right. Busy out there.
Very.
The school holidays make everything slower, I think.
They do. Let us get to it.
Any symptoms since I last saw you?
No. Nothing that I have noticed.
Should there have been?
No. No symptoms is what we want.
Right. But the tests. Were they all right?
I have been worrying about them all week.
They were. Your long-term sugar value is 43 millimoles per mole.
Is that a good number? It sounds high to me.
It is a good number. Your diabetes is well controlled.
Well controlled. You are sure about that.
I am. That is what the result shows.
And my kidneys? That is the part that frightens me most.
Your creatinine is normal, and there is no albumin in your urine.
So nothing's showing there?
Nothing's showing on those tests. No.
All right. That does help.
Good. So nothing changes. Continue your current treatment exactly as it is.
And I do not need anything extra. No new medicine?
No. Routine follow-up as usual.
Routine. Yes. I can manage routine.
You can. Did you finish that book you mentioned?
I did actually. The ending was better than I expected.
